title: Could you lift one lakh sheets of paper at once?
description: One sheet of paper weighs five grams. The weight of one lakh sheets is found in grams, changed to kilograms, and judged against what a person can lift. Keeko raises the doubt that one lakh sheets of five grams weigh only five hundred grams.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiply the number of sheets by the weight of one, then change grams to kilograms. Watch for students who lose zeros when multiplying a lakh by five.

source: If a single sheet of paper weighs 5 grams, could you lift one lakh sheets of paper together at the same time?
video_script.why: The child can multiply large numbers and now uses the product to judge whether a heavy load can be lifted.
video_script.substitution: Total weight is the number of sheets times the weight of one sheet; then grams are changed to kilograms.
video_script.anchor: a single sheet of paper marked 5 grams beside a tall stack of one lakh sheets
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko loses zeros when multiplying one lakh by five and gets 500 g instead of 5,00,000 g.
video_script.payoff_line: One lakh sheets of paper weigh five hundred kilograms, which is too heavy to lift at once

final_answer.value: No, one lakh sheets weigh 500 kg
final_answer.spoken: no, one lakh sheets weigh five hundred kilograms

maths_rules: 500 kg is far more than a person can lift at once
the slip: 1,00,000 x 5 = 500, which loses the zeros

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks one lakh sheets of five grams weigh five hundred grams.
That is half a kilogram, like a small packet.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But one lakh has five zeros, and five times it keeps all five zeros.
Five lakh grams is much more than five hundred.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We keep every zero of the lakh, so the weight is big.
